title: French First Republic
capsule: The French First Republic (République française) was proclaimed on 21 September 1792, when the newly elected National Convention abolished the monarchy following the storming of the Tuileries; Louis XVI was tried and executed in January 1793. Within this period the Republic fought the War of the First Coalition while passing through its most radical phase, the Terror of 1793-1794 under the Committee of Public Safety led by Robespierre, whose fall in Thermidor (July 1794) ushered in the more conservative Thermidorian Reaction. By the close of this window the Convention had given way in 1795 to the Directory, the five-man executive that would govern the Republic for the remainder of the decade.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Metropolitan French territory is well-defined; the republic's external boundaries changed continuously as revolutionary armies annexed neighboring territories, making a fixed territorial polygon a significant approximation.
